title: Derived coefficient change respects contraction of an absolute-Frobenius factor
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $Y$ be a scheme of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p], let $v:Y\to Y$ be any scheme endomorphism, let $b\geq0$ be an integer, and put $H=F_Y^b$ for absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Let $u:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings. Use the ordinary unbounded constant-coefficient categories $D_R=D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and ordinary derived scalar extension $T:D_A\to D_B$, $T(K)=K\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For any endomorphism $h$ of $Y$, let
$$c_{h,K}:Lh_B^*(TK)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(Lh_A^*K)$$
be the inverse comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), transported by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] to ordinary constant coefficients, with the normalization of [def-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-comparison]. For $R=A,B$ set $V_R=Lv_R^*$, $P_R=LH_R^*$ and $S_R=L(v\circ H)_R^*$. Let $d_R:S_R\xrightarrow{\sim}P_RV_R$ be the canonical compositor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and $t_R=\tau_R^{(b)}:P_R\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ the specified absolute-Frobenius trivialization [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. Define the contraction $e_R:S_R\xrightarrow{\sim}V_R$ by $e_{R,K}=t_{R,V_RK}\circ d_{R,K}$. Then for every $K\in D_A$,
$$T(e_{A,K})\circ c_{v\circ H,K}=c_{v,K}\circ e_{B,TK}$$
as morphisms $S_BTK\to TV_AK$ in $D_B$. This holds for arbitrary $v$, including noninvertible endomorphisms, and requires no annihilator prime to $p$, coefficient flatness, finite Tor amplitude, boundedness, or constructibility. The exponent $b=0$ is included with the canonical identity-pullback unitor.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] to the ordered pair $H:Y\to Y$, $v:Y\to Y$. Its composition law, after taking inverse comparisons and using the canonical compositors $d_R$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], reads $$T(d_{A,K})\circ c_{v\circ H,K}=c_{H,V_AK}\circ P_B(c_{v,K})\circ d_{B,TK}.$$ Here [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] identify the finite discrete coefficient rings with the ordinary constant rings, and [def-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-comparison] fixes the normalization of the transported comparisons. Transport the entire composition equality through these same identifications. The order is $P_RV_R$, since pullback is contravariant. No inverse to $v$ is involved.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-coefficient-naturality] with $X=Y$, exponent $b$, and object $V_AK$. It gives $$T(t_{A,V_AK})\circ c_{H,V_AK}=t_{B,TV_AK}.$$ All its hypotheses hold: the same characteristic-$p$ scheme, finite commutative rings and unital map are in use, and its $c$ is the same normalized inverse comparison. The object $V_AK$ is unrestricted in the ordinary unbounded derived category.

proof.text: The trivialization $t_B:P_B\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}$ is a natural isomorphism by [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-coefficient-naturality]. Its naturality at $c_{v,K}:V_BTK\to TV_AK$ says $$t_{B,TV_AK}\circ P_B(c_{v,K})=c_{v,K}\circ t_{B,V_BTK}.$$ Expand $e_A=t_AV_A\circ d_A$, use functoriality of $T$, and substitute Steps 1 and 2 followed by this naturality equality. The result is $$T(e_{A,K})\circ c_{v\circ H,K}=c_{v,K}\circ t_{B,V_BTK}\circ d_{B,TK}=c_{v,K}\circ e_{B,TK}.$$ This calculation only uses composition and naturality. It includes $b=0$: Step 2 is the identity comparison with the identity-pullback unitor; Steps 1 and 3 retain their unitors. No flatness, prime-to-$p$ or boundedness assumption has entered.
